questions.question: In a production linear program $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, row $i'$ describes a resource with capacity $b_{i'}$ and column $j'$ a product. What does raising the technology coefficient $a_{i',j'}$ by $\delta>0$ mean?
options: $\delta$ more units of resource $i'$ become available to the whole plan
Each unit of product $j'$ earns $\delta$ more profit than before
Each unit of product $j'$ now uses $\delta$ more units of resource $i'$
Each unit of resource $i'$ becomes worth $\delta$ more at the optimum

questions.question: In the optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with optimal basis $\mathcal{B}^*$ and basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, an entry $a_{i',j'}$ in the column of a basic variable $x_{j'}$ ($j'\in\mathcal{B}^*$) is changed. How is the effect of the change determined?
options: $\boldsymbol{B}$ itself changes, so $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ and the whole tableau may change; solve the program again
Only the reduced cost of $x_{j'}$ could change, and it stays $0$ since $x_{j'}$ is basic; nothing changes
Only the basic values $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ change; the reduced costs and $\boldsymbol{y}^*$ stay as before
Apply the test $\bar{c}_{j'}+\delta\,y_{i'}^*\geq0$ with $\bar{c}_{j'}=0$, so every $\delta\geq0$ is harmless

questions.question: At an optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*$, a nonbasic product $x_{j'}$ with profit $c_{j'}$ has reduced cost $\bar{c}_{j'}=-c_{j'}+\sum_i y_i^*a_{i,j'}$ (its objective-row entry). What does $\bar{c}_{j'}$ measure?
options: The profit $c_{j'}$ minus the value at the shadow prices of the resources one unit uses
The value at the shadow prices of the resources one unit uses, minus its profit $c_{j'}$
The shadow price of the resource in which product $j'$ has its largest coefficient
The total value $\sum_i y_i^*a_{i,j'}$ of the resources that one unit of product $j'$ uses

questions.question: In the optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, an entry $a_{i',j'}$ in the column of a nonbasic variable $x_{j'}$ is changed, all other data fixed. Which entries of the tableau change?
options: The basic values $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$, since constraint $i'$ now has a new left-hand side
The dual solution $\boldsymbol{c}_{\mathcal{B}}^{\top}\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$, since row $i'$ of $\boldsymbol{A}$ has changed
The reduced costs of all variables with a nonzero entry in row $i'$ of $\boldsymbol{A}$
Only the column of $x_{j'}$: its entries $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}'$ and its reduced cost

questions.question: At an optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $x_{j'}$ is nonbasic with reduced cost $\bar{c}_{j'}\geq0$ (objective-row entry) and row $i'$ has shadow price $y_{i'}^*>0$. How does the sign of a change $\delta$ of $a_{i',j'}$ affect optimality of the basis $\mathcal{B}^*$?
options: Every $\delta<0$ keeps $\mathcal{B}^*$ optimal; a large enough $\delta>0$ destroys optimality
Every $\delta$ keeps $\mathcal{B}^*$ optimal, since the coefficient multiplies $x_{j'}=0$
Every $\delta>0$ keeps $\mathcal{B}^*$ optimal; a large enough $\delta<0$ destroys optimality
Exactly the $\delta$ with $\lvert\delta\rvert\leq\bar{c}_{j'}$ keep $\mathcal{B}^*$ optimal

questions.question: For $\max Z=6x_1+5x_2+4x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+x_3\leq8$, $2x_1+x_2+3x_3\leq12$, $x_1+2x_2+2x_3\leq14$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the optimal tableau has objective row $(0,0,3\mid4,1,0\mid44)$ (columns $x_1,x_2,x_3$; then $s_1,s_2,s_3$; then right-hand side). If $a_{23}$ falls from $3$ to $1$, what is the new reduced cost of $x_3$?

For $\max Z=6x_1+5x_2+4x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+x_3\leq8$, $2x_1+x_2+3x_3\leq12$, $x_1+2x_2+2x_3\leq14$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the optimal basis $\{x_1,x_2,s_3\}$ gives $\boldsymbol{x}^*=(4,4,0)$, $Z^*=44$, shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(4,1,0)$ and reduced cost $\bar{c}_3=3$. What happens when $a_{13}$ rises from $1$ to $5$?
options: The basis stays optimal: $\bar{c}_3$ becomes $19$ and $Z^*$ stays $44$
The basis stays optimal, but $Z^*$ falls to $44-4\cdot4=28$
$\bar{c}_3$ becomes $3-4\cdot4=-13$, so $x_3$ enters the basis
The program must be solved again, as constraint $1$ is binding at $\boldsymbol{x}^*$

questions.question: For $\max Z=3x_1+5x_2+6x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+4x_3\leq9$, $x_1+3x_2+2x_3\leq13$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the optimal basis is $\{x_1,x_2\}$ with $\boldsymbol{x}^*=(7,2,0)$ and shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(2,1)$. Which single change can be judged by checking one updated reduced cost, without solving the program again?
options: $a_{11}$ from $1$ to $2$, because row $1$ has the larger shadow price
$a_{22}$ from $3$ to $4$, because $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ still gives $x_2=2$
$a_{21}$ from $1$ to $2$, because $x_1$ has the reduced cost $0$ to update
$a_{23}$ from $2$ to $1$, because $x_3$ is nonbasic at $\boldsymbol{x}^*$

questions.question: For $\max Z=6x_1+5x_2+4x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+x_3\leq8$, $2x_1+x_2+3x_3\leq12$, $x_1+2x_2+2x_3\leq14$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with slacks $s_1,s_2,s_3$, the optimal basis $\{x_1,x_2,s_3\}$ has shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(4,1,0)$ and reduced cost $\bar{c}_3=3$. Which entries of the column of $x_3$ can take any real value while this basis stays optimal?
options: Only $a_{13}$, since $y_1^*=4$ is the largest shadow price
Only $a_{33}$, since row $3$ has shadow price $y_3^*=0$
$a_{23}$ and $a_{33}$, since $y_2^*$ and $y_3^*$ are below $\bar{c}_3=3$
All three, since $x_3=0$ makes its whole column irrelevant

questions.question: At an optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, with basis matrix $\boldsymbol{B}$, changing $a_{i',j'}$ for a nonbasic $x_{j'}$ makes its reduced cost negative (objective-row entry; negative means $Z$ can improve). How should the analysis continue?
options: Restart with the Big-M method, since the current basic solution may now be infeasible
Stop: a negative reduced cost after such a change shows that the program is unbounded
Pivot $x_{j'}$ in using its old column $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}$, since $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}$ is unchanged
Pivot $x_{j'}$ in from the current, still feasible tableau, using $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{A}_{j'}'$

questions.question: At an optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, $x_{j'}$ is nonbasic with reduced cost $\bar{c}_{j'}$ (objective-row entry) and row $i'$ has shadow price $y_{i'}^*$. What is the new reduced cost if $c_{j'}$ rises by $\delta$, and if instead $a_{i',j'}$ rises by $\delta$?
options: It becomes $\bar{c}_{j'}-\delta$, and $\bar{c}_{j'}+\delta\,y_{i'}^*$ respectively
It becomes $\bar{c}_{j'}+\delta$, and $\bar{c}_{j'}+\delta\,y_{i'}^*$ respectively
It becomes $\bar{c}_{j'}-\delta$, and $\bar{c}_{j'}-\delta\,y_{i'}^*$ respectively
It becomes $\bar{c}_{j'}-\delta$, and $\bar{c}_{j'}+\delta$ respectively

questions.question: At an optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the slack variable of row $i'$ is basic with value $s>0$, so $y_{i'}^*=0$, and $x_{j'}$ is basic with value $x_{j'}^*>0$. The entry $a_{i',j'}$ rises by $\delta>0$. Which statement is correct?
options: The basis stays optimal for every $\delta>0$, as a row with shadow price $0$ never matters
For every $\delta>0$ only $Z^*$ changes, by $\delta\,y_{i'}^*x_{j'}^*=0$, so $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ stays optimal
The old optimum violates row $i'$ once $\delta x_{j'}^*>s$, so the program must be solved again
The old optimum stays feasible for every $\delta>0$, as $x_{j'}$ only becomes less attractive

questions.question: A firm solves $\max Z=7x_A+8x_B+7x_D$ subject to labour $x_A+2x_B+2x_D\leq10$, material $x_A+x_B+x_D\leq9$, machine time $2x_A+x_B+x_D\leq11$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$. The optimal plan $(4,3,0)$ has shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(3,0,2)$. For which labour use per unit of $D$ (now $2$ hours) does this plan stay optimal?
options: At least $1$ hour, since the reduced cost $1$ allows a cut of $1$
At least $\tfrac{5}{3}$ hours, since the reduced cost $1$ allows a cut of $\tfrac{1}{3}$
At least $\tfrac{3}{2}$ hours, since the reduced cost $1$ allows a cut of $\tfrac{1}{2}$
At most $\tfrac{7}{3}$ hours, since the reduced cost $1$ allows a rise of $\tfrac{1}{3}$

questions.question: For $\max Z=3x_1+5x_2+6x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+4x_3\leq9$, $x_1+3x_2+2x_3\leq13$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2)$ has shadow prices $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(2,1)$ and reduced cost $\bar{c}_3=4$ (objective-row entry). The column of $x_3$ changes at once to $a_{13}=3$ and $a_{23}=-1$, all other data fixed. What follows?
options: The basis stays optimal, since each change on its own keeps the reduced cost of $x_3$ nonnegative
The basis stays optimal, since the new reduced cost of $x_3$ is $4+2\cdot1+1\cdot3=9$
The basis stays optimal, since the new reduced cost of $x_3$ is $4-1-3=0$
The basis is no longer optimal, since the new reduced cost of $x_3$ is $-6+2\cdot3+1\cdot(-1)=-1$

questions.question: For $\max Z=8x_1+3x_2+3x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+x_3\leq7$, $3x_1+x_2+3x_3\leq15$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}-\tfrac{1}{2}&\tfrac{1}{2}\\\tfrac{3}{2}&-\tfrac{1}{2}\end{bmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}=(4,3)$. Lowering $a_{23}$ from $3$ to $0$ makes $x_3$ enter. Which column and leaving variable result?
options: Column $(-\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{3}{2})$; $x_2$ leaves, with ratio $3/\tfrac{3}{2}=2$
Column $(1,0)$; $x_1$ leaves, with ratio $4/1=4$
Column $(-\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{3}{2})$; $x_1$ leaves, with ratio $4/(-\tfrac{1}{2})=-8$
Column $(-\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2})$; $x_2$ leaves, with ratio $3/\tfrac{1}{2}=6$

questions.question: At an optimal tableau of $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the slack variable of row $i'$ is basic with value $0$, so row $i'$ is binding at $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ and $y_{i'}^*=0$. For a nonbasic $x_{j'}$ with $\bar{c}_{j'}\geq0$, what is the effect of changing $a_{i',j'}$ by $\delta$?
options: A change $\delta<-\bar{c}_{j'}$ breaks optimality, because row $i'$ is binding at $\boldsymbol{x}^*$
The basis stays optimal for every $\delta$, since the reduced cost becomes $\bar{c}_{j'}+\delta\cdot0$
The shortcut fails at a degenerate corner point, so the program has to be solved again
The basis stays optimal, but $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ may become infeasible because row $i'$ is binding

questions.question: For $\max Z=\boldsymbol{c}^{\top}\boldsymbol{x}$ subject to $\boldsymbol{A}\boldsymbol{x}\leq\boldsymbol{b}$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$ with optimal solution $\boldsymbol{x}^*$, value $Z^*$ and $x_{j'}^*=0$ nonbasic, the entry $a_{i',j'}$ is changed by some $\delta\neq0$. Which statement about the new optimal value is correct (count an unbounded program as value $+\infty$)?
options: For $\delta>0$ it falls by $\delta\,y_{i'}^*$, since resource $i'$ is now used more
It equals $Z^*$ for every $\delta$, since the basis stays feasible for every $\delta$
It can drop below $Z^*$, since the feasible region changes with $a_{i',j'}$
It is never below $Z^*$, since $\boldsymbol{x}^*$ stays feasible with value $Z^*$

questions.question: For $\max Z=2x_1+3x_2$ subject to $x_1+x_2\leq4$, $x_1+3x_2\leq6$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, both $x_1$ and $x_2$ are basic at the optimum $\boldsymbol{x}^*=(3,1)$ with $Z^*=9$ and $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(\tfrac{3}{2},\tfrac{1}{2})$. If $a_{11}$ rises from $1$ to $2$, what is the new optimal value?

For $\max Z=3x_1+5x_2+6x_3$ subject to $x_1+x_2+4x_3\leq9$, $x_1+3x_2+2x_3\leq13$, $\boldsymbol{x}\geq\boldsymbol{0}$, the optimal basis $(x_1,x_2)$ has $\boldsymbol{B}^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}\tfrac{3}{2}&-\tfrac{1}{2}\\-\tfrac{1}{2}&\tfrac{1}{2}\end{bmatrix}$, $\boldsymbol{x}^*=(7,2,0)$, $Z^*=31$, $\boldsymbol{y}^*=(2,1)$ and $\bar{c}_3=4$. Which statement holds after $a_{13}$ falls from $4$ to $2$?
options: The basis stays optimal with $Z^*=31$, and $(0,2,\tfrac{7}{2})$ is a second optimal solution
The basis is no longer optimal, since the reduced cost of $x_3$ is no longer positive
The basis stays optimal, and $(7,2,0)$ is the only optimal solution, as $Z^*$ is unchanged
$x_3$ enters at $\tfrac{7}{2}$, and $Z^*$ rises to $31+4\cdot\tfrac{7}{2}=45$ at $(0,2,\tfrac{7}{2})$
